sample.note: The same capped subsample is used for all three models, so the coefficients are comparable and the difference between them is not a difference of sample.

linear_probability_model_with_lender_dum.note: For a linear model the within-transformation and the dummy-variable parameterisation give identical slope coefficients, so this is the estimand the demeaned-logit code was trying to reach, estimated in a form where the transformation is valid.  Standard errors are clustered by lender.

logit_with_lender_dummies.note: the same lender dummies in a logistic regression: a different estimator of the same population parameter, on a different scale

logit_without_lender_fixed_effects_same_.note: the same model without the lender dummies, on the same rows, so the two are directly comparable

interpretation.note: The linear probability model reports a probability difference in percentage points; the logistic models report an odds ratio.  A negative probability difference and an odds ratio below one are the same finding expressed on different scales.
